parts.note: the idiom 'cut the ...' means stop chattering; the clue's 'it' stands for the noisy chatter you are told to cut

explanation.surface: An order to snip something and stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut the cackle' is a British idiom meaning stop talking and get on with it; the 'it' of the clue is the word that completes that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: noisy chatter is what you cut when told to stop talking and keep quiet.

definitions.meaning: the actors in a play, taken together
a throw, as in pitching a ball or a fishing line

explanation.definitionFit: A play's company of actors is its cast, and to cast is to throw or pitch something.

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit concentrate diluted to drink

explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a cordial welcome is a friendly one, and a cordial is a sweet diluted soft drink.

parts.note: not an archer pulling a bowstring but something that draws the curved outline of the upper lip, known as a Cupid's bow

explanation.surface: Who pulls back the string on the love god's bow?
explanation.walkthrough: The Cupid's bow is the double curve of the upper lip; 'drawer' means something that draws an outline, not one who pulls a bowstring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic use: a coloured stick traces the outline of the lips, including the curve called Cupid's bow.

clue.text: Am taken aback, unhappy about the flag's position

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the little word 'Am' is turned round

parts.note: taken as written before turning

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for unhappy is placed around 'the'

parts.note: unhappy means sad
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shocked and gloomy about where a flag is flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' and 'about' are both indicators here: one turns the first word round, the other wraps the gloomy word around 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag is flown at the top of a mast, which is the meaning of this nautical word.

parts.note: not sewing but healing treatment carried out with needles

explanation.surface: Sewing done to mend or put things right.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the Chinese therapy inserts fine needles into the body to relieve pain and illness.

clue.text: Stroll round to see the cave-dwellers

indicators.note: round suggests letters turned about and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Take a walk about to have a look at people living in caves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' rearranges the letters of STROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore: these ugly giants or dwarfs of Scandinavian legend live in caves or under bridges.

clue.text: No one has time to set up the paper

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide

explanation.surface: Nobody has a moment to get the newspaper typeset.
explanation.walkthrough: NO + I + TIDE gives NOITIDE, and 'to set up' turns the whole thing to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: a newspaper's printing for a given day or time is referred to as an issue or a particular printing.

indicators.note: orders here means puts in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Secret agents receive instructions in sealed envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' rearranges the letters of GET SEALED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: representatives sent to act on behalf of others are agents or envoys at a conference.

parts.note: not a Hollywood celebrity's partner but what sits with the stars on the US flag, the Stars and ...

explanation.surface: Who goes about with a famous US celebrity?
explanation.walkthrough: The American flag is the Stars and Stripes, so each star's companion on it is a band of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the US flag, the Stars and Stripes, pairs its stars with bands of red and white.

clue.text: Getting out stupidly in Test is a learning experience

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for a test

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: stupidly means done in a muddled way, so the letters of 'out' are jumbled

explanation.surface: Being dismissed foolishly in a Test match teaches a batsman a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting out' looks like a batsman being dismissed, but 'out' is anagram fodder. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a teaching session with a tutor is a learning experience for the student.

clue.text: Tower of Pisa, say, is of architectural interest

definitions.text: Tower of Pisa, say, is of architectural interest

parts.words: Tower of Pisa, say, is of architectural interest
parts.note: the leaning tower 'lists' to one side, and a structure protected for its architectural interest is formally 'listed' in Britain

explanation.surface: The famous tower in Italy is an important piece of architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a building of special architectural interest is officially listed and protected; to list also means to lean, as the Pisa tower does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: in Britain a protected historic structure is officially 'listed', and the tilting Pisa tower also lists.

parts.note: uncalled for here means never collected, as post nobody calls to pick up, rather than unwarranted

explanation.surface: This kind of letter-writing is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: Undeliverable post that nobody collects goes to a dead letter office; the clue also suggests rules no longer enforced.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: post that cannot be delivered and is never claimed by anyone is given this name.

indicators.note: produce here means make something new from the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A talk may cause listeners to react against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' rearranges LECTURE CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unwillingness or hesitancy is a reaction of being averse to doing something.

indicators.note: restored means put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Things back to normal at a profitable company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' rearranges NORMALITY. This is the body that produces British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the British state body that literally manufactures coins is a moneymaking organisation.

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage
a nit is a fool or twit

explanation.surface: A single toff who is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a single thing or quantity is one, a discrete item.

clue.text: Yet he enjoys some standing at meetings

definitions.text: Yet he enjoys some standing at meetings

parts.words: Yet he enjoys some standing at meetings
parts.note: standing means status, but he is the one at meetings who stays seated

explanation.surface: Even so, this man has a certain status at gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'yet' is the joke: he has standing (status) though his title suggests he sits down.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the person presiding over a meeting holds the senior status while seated.

indicators.note: cooked means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S taken as letters

explanation.surface: Amy has prepared the root vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges AMYS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: these starchy tropical tubers are eaten as vegetables, like sweet potatoes.

indicators.note: working means being worked on or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Merely doing a job wore me out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' rearranges TIRED ME. 'Just' is an adjective meaning deserved, not the adverb 'only'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a just reward is one that is deserved or earned.

indicators.note: on board means aboard ship, so the merriment goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded, and SS is the abbreviation for steamship
laughter is merriment

explanation.surface: News reports bring amusement aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatches' looks like a noun for news reports but is the verb meaning kills; 'on board' is the usual crossword signal for going inside a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dispatch someone is to kill them, as an abattoir does.

clue.text: For example, rising in the morning with enthusiasm

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the word for the morning

parts.note: early is in the morning

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: EG abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Getting up at dawn keenly, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example, rising' reads like a morning routine, but the abbreviation goes up and sits inside the word for early hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doing something keenly is doing it with enthusiasm.

parts.note: a mode is a style or fashion
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A fresh look for the fleet's uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: RN stands for the Royal Navy, Britain's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something modern is new or up to date.

definitions.meaning: the Tolkien fantasy adapted for cinema
a fighter who rules the boxing rings, jokingly titled

explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: Tolkien's epic became a famous film trilogy, and a top boxer would be master of the rings.

clue.text: Present the woman's beginning to expect

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gift is what the lady starts to expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being present means being in this place, in attendance.

clue.text: Suffering from a lack of balance?

definitions.text: Suffering from a lack of balance?

parts.words: Suffering from a lack of balance?
parts.note: not physically unsteady but with a bank balance below zero, overdrawn

explanation.surface: Someone is unsteady on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Debts used to be written in red ink, so an overdrawn account is in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an account short of money, overdrawn, is said to be in the red.

clue.text: Come out East and join up

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
to merge is to join up

explanation.surface: Appear from the east and enlist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to come out into view is to appear or come forth.

clue.text: Insisted order must be a good order

indicators.note: order means arrange, so the letters of the word before it are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A demand that everything be kept shipshape.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'order' rearranges INSISTED; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: neatness means everything is kept in good order.

clue.text: Enemy Zulu leader going round causing ferment

indicators.note: going round suggests spinning about, so the letters are mixed up
a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hostile Zulu chief prowls about stirring up unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' takes Z from Zulu, and 'going round' rearranges ENEMY plus Z. 'Ferment' is a noun here: an agent causing fermentation.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sense: a ferment was a substance like yeast that brings about fermentation, now called a biological catalyst.
